name: Great Lakes 2T-1A Sport Trainer
manufacturer: Great Lakes Aircraft Company / WACO Classic Aircraft
summary: Compact two-seat 1929 sport trainer and aerobatic biplane, put back into production in the 1970s and again in 2011; popular with weekend aerobats.

wings: Single-bay staggered biplane with an upper wing that is swept back
engines: Cowled flat-four Lycoming on most surviving examples (early ones had an inline Cirrus)
fuselage: Fixed tailwheel gear with short main legs
tail: Enlarged tail with a large rounded rudder

tellTales: Compact tandem-seat open-cockpit biplane with a cowled flat engine
Swept-back upper wing on a short-span biplane
Slim fuselage with large rounded tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The Pitts is smaller and stubbier; the Great Lakes has a longer, slimmer fuselage and a more pronounced upper-wing sweep.
The Stearman is much larger with a bare radial engine; the Great Lakes is small with a cowled flat engine.
The Stampe has a narrower nose sloping down to an inline engine; the Great Lakes has a wider, blunter cowl over a flat-four.
